rule: จักร is the discus, and its senses are what the discus looks like and does. Sense 1, the weapon itself, takes the things that ARE discuses: กงจักร (the toothed ring), ขว้างจักร (the thrown disc of athletics) and จักรกรี (discus and trident, the Chakri emblem). Sense 2, anything round like a wheel, takes the circle words — the wheel of จักรยาน, the circle of stars in ดาราจักร (thai-full glosses its จักร as วงกลม), the circle of the zodiac in จักรราศี, and the circle of rule in อาณาจักร. Sense 3, the powered toothed wheel, takes ใบจักร, the blade of a ship's driven wheel. Sense 6, a cycle coming round again, takes วัฏจักร and มหาจักร, the sixty-year round.

notes.h2: 2026-10-05 — จักร, ช้าง, แกง (33 filed)
notes.text:
**Rule.** จักร is the discus, and its senses are what the discus looks like and
does. 1, the weapon, takes the words for things that ARE discuses. 2, round like a
wheel, takes the circles. 3, the powered toothed wheel, takes the ship's driven
wheel. 6, a cycle that comes round again, takes the cycles.

notes.h2: 2026-10-05 — จักร, ช้าง, แกง (33 filed)
notes.text:
The head is itself a Sanskrit loan, so I checked every etymology before filing.
None of the ten opens with ยืมมาจาก. Each reads X + จักร, so each is a compound on
the record. (จักรวาล and ธรรมจักร were tagged false-split by an earlier pass. I left
them as they are.)

notes.h2: 2026-10-05 — จักร, ช้าง, แกง (33 filed)
notes.text:
**Unsure.**
* **อาณาจักร → 2.** The Pali is āṇācakka, which could be read two ways. One is
  the CIRCLE of rule: Sanskrit cakra also means a district or realm, and that is
  sense 2's circle. The other is the sovereign's WHEEL of command, the
  cakravartin's discus, which would be sense 1. I took 2. If a source says the
  wheel of the wheel-turning king, it moves to 1.
* **จักรกรี → 1, though it is a retired spelling.** Its gloss is *รูปเลิกใช้ของ
  จักรี*. Under the 9/18 note, retired spellings are judged per head. thai-full
  gives its own etymology as จักร + กรี, discus and trident, the two weapons of
  the Chakri emblem. So the retired form is the one that really contains this
  head's sense 1, and I filed it there rather than tagging it `spelling-variant`.
* **ใบจักร → 3 rather than 4.** The ship's wheel is a power-driven rotating
  wheel, which is sense 3 exactly. Sense 4, "a machine", would also hold it.
* **มหาจักร → 6** on its 60-year-period gloss (five turns of Jupiter). Its first
  RID gloss is a Thai medicine name, and that gloss does not decide a sense.
* **ขว้างจักร → 1.** The athletic discus is the thrown disc. 2 is the defensible
  alternative.

notes.h2: 2026-10-05 — จักร, ช้าง, แกง (33 filed)
notes.text:
**Left unfiled.** จักรพันธุ์ (`personal-name`) and จตุจักร (`toponym`): จักร has no
name-use sense, and I will not invent one. These are the same position as
แกดำ and กองแขก.
